periods.name: November 2025
periods.summary: The month potpie-ui's dark-mode and input-contrast complaints pile up, just before the SSO and Azure work of December.
periods.description: November 2025 is the earliest window this graph carries activities for, and it is dominated by potpie-ui frontend defects reported in quick succession: issues #205, #207 and #209 all describe the same shared shadcn Input primitive rendering as greyed out because it hardcodes placeholder:text-black, the symptom tracked as bug_pattern potpie-ui-input-greyed-out and adjacent to the dark-mode contrast pattern. It is the run-up month to December's SSO rollout and the Azure/AKS production cutover. Search terms: November 2025, input box greyed out, dark mode contrast, early UI issues, pre-Azure month.

periods.name: December 2025
periods.summary: SSO lands in potpie, the Azure/AKS cutover finishes, and potpie-workflows is bootstrapped.
periods.description: December 2025 is the month the auth story got rebuilt and the platform finished moving to Azure. In potpie, Yash Krishan shipped the SSO implementation (#506) followed by a run of correction PRs — SSO/email auth fixes (#544), Firebase-UID-consistent GitHub linking (#546), and handling for a GitHub account already linked to another user (#549); Deeptendu Santra fixed potpie graph creation (#531) and the GitHub token fallback (#515), while Deepesh Genani chased duplicate logging out of supervisord.conf (#540) and fixed staging logging (#538). Infra-side, the terraform-azure work from October (potpie-aks in Central India, PostgreSQL moved off azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server into a Kubernetes StatefulSet per POSTGRESQL_MIGRATION.md) reached production cutover, which is where the alembic migration-lock incident happened. potpie-ui had a heavy 41-commit month and potpie-workflows saw its first 12 commits. Search terms: December 2025, SSO rollout, Azure cutover, month of the postgres migration lock.

periods.name: January 2026
periods.summary: potpie-workflows sprint (65 commits), VS Code tunnel work, agent revamp, and the first big Vanta CVE wave.
periods.description: January 2026 was the workflows-and-editor month. potpie-workflows took 65 commits building the recipes store, celery_recipe_subscriber and spec/codegen streaming; potpie-vscode-extension took 33 commits around local tunnel setup, dynamic port routing and AuthManager stability (Yash Krishan, nndn). In potpie itself Nandan shipped the agent revamp (#556) and agent improvements (#557), Yash Krishan added work-email validation for SSO (#551) and bumped fastmcp/langchain-core for security (#553), and Shambhavi Shinde ran two Vanta vulnerability sweeps (#562, #563) plus the aiohttp 3.13.3 bump for CVE-2025-69223 (#564). Operationally this is the month the workflows ingress hostname lost its TLS SAN on the new AKS cluster. Search terms: January 2026, workflows sprint, VS Code tunnel, Vanta wave, cert expiry month.

periods.name: February 2026
periods.summary: Peak-velocity month across every repo: codegen agents, spec gen, repo manager, v1.0.0, and a production config rollback.
periods.description: February 2026 is the busiest month in the whole record — potpie 43 commits, potpie-ui 104, potpie-workflows 88, potpie-vscode-extension 21. Deeptendu Santra landed the repo manager with parsing logic (#566), logfire (#574) and codegen agents + tools in workflows (#38); Deepesh Genani built worktree-only parsing with bulletproof recreation (#607), PR tools in the codegen agent (#619) and the parsing-failure email alert (#623); Shambhavi Shinde added the Spec Gen agent (#597) and repo pagination (#621); Kshitij Mishra redesigned the README and architecture diagram. potpie v1.0.0 was tagged on 2026-02-23. It is also the month prod deployment config changes from 4c05277b had to be reverted (#618) and the Celery recipe queue backed up badly enough that a purge script was written and then deliberately removed from the repo. Search terms: February 2026, peak velocity, codegen agents, celery backlog, prod rollback.

periods.name: March 2026
periods.summary: Test-suite and reliability month: neo4j/httpx leak fix, 50% coverage gate, stress tests, Stripe subscriptions.
periods.description: March 2026 turned toward reliability and quality gates. Yash Krishan added the test suite structure with parsing tests, automation and stress runs (#680), a 50% coverage target with a PR regression gate (#695), and fixed the Neo4j connection leak surfaced by the httpx monitor (#672) plus an UnboundLocalError for Repo in setup_project_directory (#697). Shambhavi Shinde integrated subscriptions and Stripe message-usage reporting (#709) and added a local API-key fallback via the local secret encryption env var (#679); Deepesh Genani truncated large tool results and removed their DB persistence (#716); Hari E ran the Vanta medium and high sweeps (#696, #707). Operationally, the Neo4j connection pool exhausted during a large repo backfill and that is the incident the httpx monitor fix closed out. Search terms: March 2026, neo4j pool exhaustion, coverage gate, stress tests, subscription billing.

periods.name: April 2026
periods.summary: Rust parsing module, ColBERT embeddings, deep-agent plan generation in workflows, and test seed data.
periods.description: April 2026 was a performance month. Deeptendu Santra shipped the new Rust parsing module (#735), fixed its Docker build (#744), and followed with faster parsing plus ColBERT embeddings (#746); Nandan added data seeding for tests (#733) in both potpie and potpie-workflows; Shambhavi Shinde added the backend mode-switch API with DB update (#728) and cleared the full critical/high/medium/low Vanta set (#734, #54). In potpie-workflows the spec generator was reworked around deep agents, the plan-generation pipeline was unified for research/author/diagrams, and Potpie read/grep/glob/bash tools were wired into the hybrid research agent with ripgrep. potpie v1.0.2 shipped on 2026-04-22. PgBouncer OOMKills on staging happened in this window. Search terms: April 2026, rust parser, colbert, deep agents, plangen, pgbouncer oomkill.

periods.name: May 2026
periods.summary: The context-engine merge lands in potpie, a new observability package replaces ad-hoc logging, CI is hardened.
periods.description: May 2026 is the pivot month: Nandan merged Feat/context engine into potpie (#749) and then spent days repairing CI failures after the merge (#765), while potpie-ui absorbed the same change across five feat/context-engine and feat/events-revamp merges into staging. Yash Krishan shipped the new logging + Sentry + Logfire observability package (#785) and switched the codebase onto it (#790), and hardened the prod Jenkins deployment pipelines (#752); Deepesh Genani added the optional Hatchet durable agent runtime (#816) and routed regenerate through backend selection (#817), plus the torch 2.11.0 -> 2.12.0 bump for Python 3.13.8 (#793). Shambhavi Shinde ran the single largest security wave of the year across potpie and potpie-ui (#766, #770, #773, #779, #784, #788, #812 and the fix/critical-vanta, fix/med-vanta, fix/high-vanta UI branches). potpie v1.1.0 and v1.1.1 shipped. Search terms: May 2026, context engine merge, observability package, jenkins hardening, vanta wave.

periods.name: June 2026
periods.summary: Context-engine build-out month: domain, backends, workbench, detached daemon, graph explorer, telemetry, and 2.0 betas.
periods.description: June 2026 was the densest engineering month in potpie (68 commits) and produced most of the shipped context-engine surface: the CE domain foundation (#903), CE backends including FalkorDB and the mutation pipeline (#910), CE application services with the workbench, V2 read surface and nudge model (#914), the CE graph workbench command surface (#915), the detached daemon and daemon runtime (#916), and the graph explorer UI (#918), followed by the mega-removal of dead CE surface and the pots reorg (#919). Deeptendu Santra deprecated the server (#851), added PostHog CLI usage instrumentation (#888) and Sentry metrics (#886), and capped the Sentry SDK below 3.0 (#938). Nihit Gupta, Shambhavi Shinde and Bharath Kumar K did a long CLI-UX pass (#863, #874, #877, #880, #937, #941, #943, #960, #964, #966, #972, #974). v2.0.0b1 and v2.0.0b3 shipped. Search terms: June 2026, context engine build-out, daemon, workbench, posthog, sentry, 2.0 beta.

periods.name: July 2026
periods.summary: potpie 2.0.0 GA, the context-core library carve-out, and the embedded-FalkorDB claim-read invisibility fix in flight.
periods.description: July 2026 opened with potpie 2.0.0 (#991) and a batch of correctness work — the include-family/graph-view vocabulary boundary (POT-1770, #985), graph read filters and text presentation honoring format/detail/relations (#995), infra-topology query-sensitive ranking (#999), and Linear CLI OAuth callback ports (#968). Mid-month Nandan carved the graph core into a potpie-context-core library, moved the CLI, daemon, MCP server and host-app services into the root package, split context-engine dependencies into per-adapter-family extras, and flattened potpie-context-core into a library-shaped package. Shambhavi Shinde upgraded MCP past high-severity advisories (#1014), exposed patched dependency floors in package metadata (#1015), and remediated the Vanta CVE set with torch 2.12.1 (#1000). The month's open operational item is the embedded-FalkorDB claim-read invisibility on falkordb_lite, fixed in PR #1002. Search terms: July 2026, 2.0.0 GA, context-core carve out, falkordb claim invisibility, current month.

activities.name: Incident — alembic migration lock during the Azure Postgres cutover
activities.summary: A long-running alembic migration held an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock during the cutover to Kubernetes Postgres, stalling mom-api writes for 41 minutes.
activities.description: During the cutover described in POSTGRESQL_MIGRATION.md — moving off azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server to the postgresql StatefulSet at postgresql.devops.svc.cluster.local — an alembic migration adding an index without CONCURRENTLY took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the conversations table while celery-api was still writing. Symptoms: 'canceling statement due to lock timeout', 'deadlock detected', mom-api 502s from the ingress, and pg_stat_activity full of rows in 'idle in transaction' behind PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode. Resolved by draining celery-api, terminating the blocking backend, and re-running the migration in a maintenance window; the fix was to require CONCURRENTLY plus a statement_timeout on schema migrations. Search for: migration lock, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, alembic stuck, pgbouncer idle in transaction, azure cutover outage.

activities.name: Incident — workflows hostname served an invalid certificate after the AKS move
activities.summary: The workflows ingress host was missing from the cert-manager Certificate SAN list on the new cluster, so TLS failed for every workflows client.
activities.description: After the AKS cutover the cert-manager Certificate in prod/cert-manager/api-certificate.yaml was reissued without the workflows hostname in its dnsNames list, exactly the class of gap the earlier 'fix: add workflows route to cert manager' change addressed by adding workflows.potpie.ai and stage-workflows.potpie.ai to the SAN list. Symptoms: 'x509: certificate is valid for production-api.potpie.ai, not workflows.potpie.ai', SSL_ERROR_BAD_CERT_DOMAIN in browsers, curl 'SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name', and workflows webhook deliveries failing at the TLS handshake before any HTTP status. Resolved by adding the SAN back, forcing a Certificate reissue from the letsencrypt-prod ClusterIssuer, and verifying the secret contents. Search for: cert-manager SAN missing, x509 certificate is valid for, workflows.potpie.ai TLS outage, letsencrypt reissue.

activities.name: Incident — Celery recipe queue backlog stalled the workflows event bus
activities.summary: Long-running codegen tasks starved the celery_recipe_subscriber queue; depth passed 4,000 messages and recipe events stopped being consumed.
activities.description: Codegen agent tasks with generous tool limits ran for tens of minutes each and monopolised every celery-api worker slot, so the recipe event queue backed up behind them and users saw specs and plans that never started. Symptoms: Redis broker list length climbing monotonically, 'Recipe stuck in QUEUED', no ToolCallPart chunks arriving on the stream, and workers showing zero prefetch availability. Mitigated by purging the broker with the throwaway scripts/clear_celery_local.py (added and deliberately removed from the repo the same week), then fixed by reducing codegen tool limits and adding no-exploration prompts to avoid timeouts, plus splitting the recipe subscriber onto its own queue. Search for: celery queue depth, recipe stuck queued, worker starvation, purge celery queues, event bus backlog.

activities.name: Incident — Neo4j connection pool exhaustion during a large repo backfill
activities.summary: A multi-thousand-file repo backfill leaked driver sessions until the Neo4j pool was exhausted and every graph read on production failed.
activities.description: Parsing a very large repository opened a Neo4j session per file task and never released it on the error path, so the bolt driver pool saturated. Symptoms: 'Unable to acquire connection from the pool within configured maximum time', neo4j driver 'ClientError: pool is closed', graph queries timing out at the API layer while Neo4j CPU sat idle, and the httpx connection monitor showing connections climbing and never returning. Resolved by restarting the neo4j-cluster servers to drop stale sessions and then permanently by the fix/neo4j-leak-httpx-monitor change (#672), which closed sessions in a finally block and added leak detection. Search for: unable to acquire connection from the pool, neo4j session leak, bolt pool exhausted, repo backfill outage.

activities.name: Incident — PgBouncer pods OOMKilled on staging after the ColBERT embedding rollout
activities.summary: Higher per-worker memory from the ColBERT embedding path pushed staging pods past their limits; PgBouncer and celery pods were OOMKilled in a loop.
activities.description: After the faster-parsing and ColBERT embeddings change went to staging, celery-api pods held large tensors while also holding pooled connections, and node memory pressure caused the kubelet to evict PgBouncer. Symptoms: pod status OOMKilled with exit code 137, CrashLoopBackOff on the pgbouncer deployment, 'server closed the connection unexpectedly' from mom-api, and pgb-hpa scaling up into the same memory ceiling. Resolved by raising the PgBouncer memory request/limit, adding a PodDisruptionBudget so the pool never dropped to zero replicas, and capping the embedding batch size per worker. Search for: OOMKilled exit code 137, CrashLoopBackOff pgbouncer, server closed the connection unexpectedly, staging memory pressure.

activities.name: Incident — Linear connector OAuth token refresh failed for all CLI users
activities.summary: Refresh tokens for the Linear integration stopped being exchanged after the client ID was baked into the wheel, breaking Linear ingestion until re-auth.
activities.description: The CLI's Linear OAuth flow stored refresh tokens issued against a client ID that changed when the Linear and GitHub OAuth client IDs were baked into the wheel at build time (#876), so every refresh returned invalid_grant. Symptoms: 'invalid_grant', 'Linear integration not connected' from an account that had connected it, `potpie source list` showing a Linear source with zero claims, and the callback listener binding an unexpected loopback port. Resolved by invalidating the stale credential records, forcing a re-auth path, and the callback-port fix in 'Fix Linear CLI OAuth callback ports' (#968); keyring credential storage had already been disabled (#923) which changed where the bad tokens were cached. Search for: invalid_grant linear, OAuth refresh failure, linear integration not connected, callback port, re-auth required.

activities.name: Incident — sentence-transformers cold start timed out fresh daemon and MCP sessions
activities.summary: First-use model load for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 exceeded the daemon startup deadline after the torch 2.12.1 bump, so early searches returned empty.
activities.description: With the torch 2.12.1 image, loading sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 on first use took long enough that the context-engine daemon's readiness deadline elapsed and MCP sessions started against a not-yet-ready embedder. Symptoms: `potpie status` reporting not ready, 'daemon did not become ready in time', semantic search returning zero results on a pot that clearly had claims, and `graph status` showing match_mode vector with no embedder dimensions. Resolved by warming the model during setup's embeddings step, raising the readiness deadline, and surfacing the active embedder {name, dimensions} beside match_mode so a cold or hashing embedder is no longer indistinguishable from a healthy one. Search for: daemon not ready, model cold start, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 slow load, empty semantic search, embedder dimensions.

activities.name: Incident — embedded FalkorDB claims anchored on node id 0 were invisible to every read surface
activities.summary: On the default falkordb_lite backend, claims anchored on a pot's first-created entity silently disappeared from reads while commit reported success.
activities.description: The embedded FalkorDB engine returns zero rows for a source-anchored traversal when the bound source node is internal id 0 — always the Repository in the standard flow — and both claim read paths plus the embedding-attach query used exactly that shape, so every miss was silent. Symptoms: `graph commit` reports success but `graph read` and the UI show nothing for the repo entity, search returns fewer claims than were written, verify readback looks clean, and no error is logged anywhere. Being fixed in PR #1002 by making claim reads edge-first (dropping endpoint-node bindings so the plan compiles to an Edge By Index Scan), turning fact_query into lexical membership with a vector overlay so an unembedded claim degrades instead of vanishing, count-verifying the embedding attach, and adding a real `graph repair --semantic-index`. Search for: claims not showing after commit, falkordb_lite invisible claims, node id 0, silent zero rows, unembedded_claim_keys.

activities.name: Alert — Postgres connection saturation during the Azure cutover
activities.summary: Grafana fired on backends waiting on locks and connection count above 90% of max_connections during the migration window.
activities.description: Monitor 'postgres-connection-saturation' fired when active backends exceeded 90% of max_connections on the Kubernetes postgresql StatefulSet and lock wait time crossed 30s, while the alembic migration held an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. It resolved on its own once the blocking backend was terminated and celery-api was drained. This is the paging signal that corresponds to the Azure cutover migration-lock incident. Search for: postgres connection saturation alert, max_connections 90%, lock wait time alert, cutover paging.

activities.name: Alert — certificate expiry warning for the workflows hostname
activities.summary: cert-manager expiry monitor warned 14 days out that no valid certificate covered the workflows ingress host.
activities.description: The certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds monitor fired a 14-day warning, but the underlying condition was worse than expiry: the reissued Certificate simply did not list the workflows hostname in its dnsNames, so cert-manager reported Ready on a certificate that did not cover the route. This alert fired two days before user-visible TLS failures and was initially dismissed as noise, which is the reason the SAN-coverage check was later added to the monitor. Search for: certificate expiry warning, cert-manager ready but wrong SAN, 14 day expiry alert, workflows route TLS.

activities.name: Alert — Celery queue depth above threshold on the recipe subscriber
activities.summary: Broker queue depth crossed 1,000 and kept climbing for 25 minutes on the workflows recipe queue.
activities.description: Monitor 'celery-queue-depth' watches the Redis broker list length per queue and fires when depth exceeds 1,000 with a positive 15-minute slope. It fired 25 minutes before users started reporting recipes stuck in QUEUED, making it the earliest signal for the workflows event-bus backlog. The alert had no per-queue breakdown at the time, so the on-call could not tell that only the recipe queue was affected. Search for: celery queue depth alert, redis broker backlog, queue slope alert, recipes stuck queued paging.

activities.name: Alert — Neo4j driver pool saturation on production
activities.summary: In-use bolt connections stayed at pool maximum for over five minutes with acquisition timeouts climbing.
activities.description: Monitor 'neo4j-pool-saturation' fires when in-use driver connections sit at max_connection_pool_size for five consecutive minutes or when connection acquisition timeouts appear in the mom-api error stream. It fired fifteen minutes before graph reads began failing outright during the large repo backfill. The httpx connection monitor added in #672 exists so this alert can distinguish a leak from genuine load. Search for: neo4j pool saturation alert, connection acquisition timeout, bolt pool max, backfill paging.

activities.name: Alert — repeated pod OOMKills on the staging namespace
activities.summary: kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason=OOMKilled fired three times in ten minutes across pgbouncer and celery-api.
activities.description: The OOMKill monitor fires on any container terminated with reason OOMKilled more than twice in a ten-minute window. On this occasion it caught pgbouncer and celery-api together, which is the signature of node-level memory pressure rather than one badly sized workload — the ColBERT embedding rollout had raised per-worker resident memory. Search for: OOMKilled alert, kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason, node memory pressure staging, exit code 137 paging.

activities.name: Alert — Sentry error-rate spike on the CLI integration flow
activities.summary: Sentry issue alert on unexpected exceptions crossing the CLI contract() boundary, dominated by invalid_grant from the Linear connector.
activities.description: Sentry is wired only for unexpected potpie CLI failures — exceptions crossing commands/_common.py::contract(), unexpected auth implementation failures in login/logout, and unexpected daemon command failures — so an error-rate spike there is always a real regression rather than user error. This alert fired when invalid_grant exceptions from the Linear token refresh became the top issue for the potpie-cli@<version> release. Search for: sentry error rate spike, contract() boundary exception, invalid_grant top issue, CLI release alert, POTPIE_SENTRY_DSN.

activities.name: Alert — p99 latency regression on the graph resolve/read path
activities.summary: p99 on the claim resolve path tripled after vector queries began falling back to full scans on the embedded backend.
activities.description: The 'graph-read-p99' monitor watches the claim resolve/read path and fired when p99 crossed 2.5s for ten minutes. The cause was query-plan shape, not load: the endpoint-bound claim queries stopped compiling to an Edge By Index Scan on falkordb_lite, so reads degraded to scans at the same time some claims went invisible. PR #1002 pins the plan shape with an EXPLAIN-based regression test precisely so this alert cannot recur silently. Search for: p99 latency alert, graph read slow, edge by index scan regression, EXPLAIN plan pin, resolve path latency.

It is the last release before the context-engine rewrite reframed the product around the graph. Search for: potpie 1.0.0, first stable release, February 2026 tag.

activities.name: Discussion — do we stay on Azure or move the graph tier back to AWS
activities.summary: Slack thread weighing the ~$250-300/month Central India AKS footprint against latency for mostly-US users.
activities.description: Thread in #infra started from the azure_cost_breakdown.csv and AZURE_RESOURCES_SUMMARY numbers: potpie-aks control plane plus a four-node Standard_D2s_v3 pool, self-hosted Postgres, Neo4j, Redis and Vault, all in Central India, against terraform-aws which still existed in the repo. The argument for staying was cost and the fact that terraform-azure was already provisioned and drifted-into-code; the argument against was p99 for US users and the fact that images still came from asia-south1-docker.pkg.dev. Outcome: stay on Azure, revisit if enterprise latency SLAs force it. Search for: azure vs aws, aks cost, central india latency, multi-cloud terraform, infra cost thread.

activities.name: Discussion — deprecate the hosted server and go CLI-first
activities.summary: The debate that ended with 'Deprecate the server and related components' (#851) and potpie-ui dropped as a submodule.
activities.description: Long thread on whether the product's centre of gravity is the hosted API or a local CLI + daemon. The case for CLI-first: the context graph is most valuable next to the code, enterprises will not ship repos to a hosted parser, and every agent harness can call a local MCP server. The case against: losing the hosted surface loses the multi-user story and the existing billing integration. Resolved in favour of CLI-first, executed as #851 (deprecate the server), #850 (remove potpie ui as submodule), #848 (remove library) and #919 (mega-removal of dead CE surface). Search for: deprecate server, CLI first decision, hosted vs local, why did we delete the API.

activities.name: Discussion — embedded falkordb_lite vs hosted Neo4j as the default backend
activities.summary: Whether zero-config embedded FalkorDB should be the default when the production stack already runs a Neo4j cluster.
activities.description: The thread that set the current default. Embedded falkordb_lite wins on onboarding — no container, no credentials, `potpie setup` just works — while the hosted Neo4j cluster in potpie-k8s-deployments has better operational tooling and a known query planner. Concerns raised at the time were exactly the ones that later bit: the embedded engine's plan shapes are less predictable, and failures in it tend to be silent rather than loud. Outcome: embedded by default, hosted selectable per pot, with a standing requirement that read paths be plan-pinned. Search for: embedded vs hosted graph, falkordb_lite default, neo4j cluster, zero config onboarding, backend selection debate.

activities.name: Discussion — should the MCP server live inside the daemon
activities.summary: Argued after the detached daemon lifecycle was restored (#889) and before the daemon runtime landed (#916).
activities.description: The question was whether the MCP server should be a separate process an agent host spawns, or a surface of the already-running detached context-engine daemon. Standalone is simpler to reason about and fails independently; in-daemon avoids a second graph-backend handle, a second embedder load, and the cold-start cost that later showed up as a real incident. Outcome: MCP served by the daemon with the CLI able to run it standalone for debugging, which is the shape shipped in #916 and finalised when the daemon, MCP server and host-app services moved into the root potpie package in July. Search for: MCP in daemon, detached daemon lifecycle, second embedder load, stdio MCP server placement.

activities.name: Discussion — how aggressive should the ingestion nudge be
activities.summary: Tuning the nudge model so an empty pot prompts ingestion without nagging agents on every call.
activities.description: Follow-up to the nudge model in the CE domain foundation (#903) and application services (#914). One side wanted the nudge on every read that returns thin results, because a pot with zero claims is the single most common failure of first-run experience; the other side pointed out that agents read constantly and a per-call nudge poisons context windows. Outcome: nudge on genuinely empty or stale scopes only, surfaced through structured output rather than prose, which is the behaviour behind 'suggest populated pot or ingestion when pot has 0 claims' (#972) and the source-resolution reason in `source list` (#937). Search for: nudge model tuning, empty pot prompt, agent context pollution, 0 claims suggestion.

activities.name: Discussion — sentence-transformers locally vs a hosted embedding API
activities.summary: Whether to keep shipping a local embedder in the wheel or call a hosted embeddings endpoint from the daemon.
activities.description: Triggered by the discovery that processes which never ran setup — fresh daemon, MCP, CI — were silently using the 256-dim hashing embedder while setup-configured installs used sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at 384 dims, making two very different quality tiers look identical. Hosted embeddings would remove the torch dependency, the wheel size and the cold start; local keeps the product usable offline and avoids sending code text to a third party, which enterprise buyers ask about first. Outcome: keep local as the default, make the active embedder visible in `graph status`, and add a real re-embed repair for dimension changes. Search for: sentence-transformers vs hosted embeddings, hashing embedder 256 dims, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384, offline embedding, wheel size torch.

activities.name: Discussion — the product / engine / core package split
activities.summary: Where the boundary sits between the potpie product package, potpie_context_engine, and the potpie-context-core library.
activities.description: The architectural thread behind the July reorg: carve the graph core into potpie-context-core with a curated API surface, move the CLI, daemon, MCP server and host-app services into the root potpie package, move context-engine packages under the potpie_context_engine namespace, and split context-engine dependencies into per-adapter-family extras. The disagreement was about whether core should be independently versioned and published (portability, enterprise embedding in pie) or vendored (one release train, no cross-version skew). Outcome: library-shaped package inside the same repo with a curated api surface, single release train for now. Search for: context-core split, package boundary, potpie_context_engine namespace, per-adapter extras, monorepo vs published library.

activities.name: Discussion — postmortem thread on silent failures in the embedded backend
activities.summary: Review thread arguing that the real defect class is silent degradation, not any single bad query.
activities.description: Postmortem discussion opened after the claim-read invisibility incident. The consensus framing: the bug was not that one Cypher shape returned zero rows, it was that four independent paths — claim read, vector read, embedding attach, verify readback — could all return empty and none of them said anything. Actions agreed: count-verify writes, escalate `commit --verify` to 'watch' when unembedded claims exist, log a warning naming the repair command on vector-query failure, and pin plan shape with EXPLAIN-based tests. Search for: silent failure postmortem, zero rows no error, verify readback watch status, unembedded_claim_keys, defect class review.
